title: A Deepawali birth in Arvi: the early years of Dattopant Thengadi
author: Editorial Desk
summary: From a small town in Wardha district to the leadership of a national movement.
body:
*Photo: Dattopant Thengadi (1920–2004)*

Dattatreya Bapurao Thengadi, known to the world as **Dattopant Thengadi**, was born in the village of **Arvi**, in the Wardha district of Maharashtra, on the day of Deepawali, **10 November 1920**. His father was Bapurao Dajiba Thengadi and his mother was Janaki Devi. The family was of modest means.

## A leader at fifteen

Leadership showed early. At fifteen he led the *Vanar Sena*, the children's wing associated with the freedom movement, and headed the student union of his municipal high school in Arvi. These were small responsibilities, but they were an early sign of an organiser.

## Study and the law

He went on to Morris College, Nagpur, and then took his law degree at the Law College in Nagpur. Those who knew him say he was at home with ideas of every kind: he read Marxist theory as carefully as he read the Indian tradition, and that habit shaped his later arguments.

## A decision in 1942

In 1942, impressed by the life and vision of Dr Keshav Baliram Hedgewar, the founder of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, he decided to become a full-time pracharak. He kept that commitment until his death in 2004.

The boy from Arvi would in time found the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh, the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh and the Swadeshi Jagaran Manch, and help to set up many other bodies. In the weeks ahead this blog will take up each of these chapters.
